Gemradcurt (H16)

Region (English scoring-table grouping): North Aelantir.

In one sentence: Save the Winter Court from the Autumnal threat, then follow Immarel as a war for survival may turn into lichdom, the Red Winter, and an eternal winter.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (53 H16-specific mission definitions plus 17 assignable shared missions) | Mission-tree update: judged by the current local files, which support EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: High (disaster, forts, finances, and provincial heating) | Early pressure: High | Expansion: High, but governance costs rise as winter spreads

1444: A Young Winter-Court Mage

The current Chinese localization renders Gemradcurt (H16) as 盖姆拉德库特; the scoring table's 盖姆拉德库尔特 is an older name. In 1444 it is already a country in the Winter Court of Eordand, not a later formable state. The country history gives it Winter Court religion, Snecboth culture, a theocracy, and capital 1775; Jhorgashirr and Eighard are historical rivals. Immarel Winterswrath has ruled since 1431 and is still a young, powerful mage in 1444. The history file gives her the Conqueror and Malevolent personalities. 1431 is the scripted accession date, not an event that occurs after the player starts the game. [Local history script]

The long hostility between the Winter and Autumn Courts shapes the opening pressure. The country narrative portrays the Winter Court as a community threatened by crusaders and seeking renewed unity. That helps explain why Immarel links survival, unification, and powerful magic, but does not excuse every later policy. The offline English Wiki has no readable main country page for Gemradcurt. A related entry on the Everfrost Prince says the connection between the Winter Fey and the source of Immarel's power is an unproven legend; it cannot be presented as established 1444 history. Another Wiki page retrospectively lists her as a Witch-King, which must not be projected backward into her starting identity. [Wiki] [Local narrative text]

From Defensive War to the Long Night

The opening missions unite the Winter Court, repel the Autumnal invaders, and seek the initiative against other seasonal powers to the south. Immarel is not only a character in the story but a powerful mage available from the start; her personal fate determines the later route. Missions and events gradually escalate the war into dependence on the Everfrost Prince's power. “The Long Night” proposes that she gain immortality through a ritual. She becomes a lich only if the relevant conditions and choices are fulfilled; Gemradcurt in 1444 is not already an undead empire. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The lich route triggers the dedicated Red Winter disaster. This is not an ordinary penalty: severe unrest and simultaneous losses to production, taxes, trade, and manpower recovery weigh on the country, alongside rebellions and several political and military crises. The player must defeat the rebels and restore stability to end this phase. If conquest has outrun the ability to finance the state and build forts, the disaster can become a long period of repayment and recovery. One player filled the country with forts to counter continuing devastation, then complained that upkeep consumed the treasury. This is a 2024–2025 play report, not a guarantee of current game values. [Local script] [Community opinion]

Surviving in Your Own Winter

The post-disaster missions do not simply send you back to siege warfare. Hearth cities, heating infrastructure, and special hearth-garrison-style provincial protection let the country maintain production and prosperity in the cold. A dedicated decision can provide a smaller, lasting degree of protection to a province hosting a qualifying mercenary, at the cost of administrative power and money. Forts offer a more general but expensive defense against devastation. This creates an unusual tension: winter can become an advantage over foreign enemies, but the country must keep paying to protect its residents, trade, and agriculture at home. [Local script]

The later campaign also features the Taigan Order, arcane education, armies of steel and bone, Winter Court knights, foreign diplomacy, and expansion into North Aelantir. In the mission narrative, Immarel tries to make distant countries accept this icy power rather than relying only on declarations of war. Yet integration of nearby cultures and faiths is not gentle. The “Cursed Laborers” mission explicitly proposes capturing intelligent woodland peoples and sending them to work camps along the rivers; the script also assigns production and culture changes to the relevant areas. This is forced labor, not merely “resource development.” By contrast, rebuilding hearth cities and restoring mage education do serve domestic public safety. Both sides coexist, making the route more interesting than a simple winter-themed villain story. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Another Route and a World-History Ending

Gemradcurt need not treat “Immarel rules forever” as its only ending. The current Eordand formation decision (H21) explicitly excludes a country that still has the “Immarel rules” flag. If she no longer rules, H16 has a mission group that points toward the ordinary Eordand formation event. Taking that general formation changes the Tag to H21 and replaces the non-generic missions. This is a conditional diversion, not an automatic imperial sequel after completing the lich storyline. This entry profiles H16 itself and does not fold the full H21 mission tree into its count of 53 H16-specific missions. [Local script]

The offline Wiki's Early Modern Eordand Timeline describes a different later worldline: the Red Winter ends, Immarel loses power, and Gemradcurt fractures. That is a historical account in the Wiki, not an inevitable ending for a player's campaign; the current Mod's missions allow Immarel's Long Night to continue. Details of a pact between the Everfrost Prince and Immarel remain between legend and mission narrative, and must not be recast as verified early history. [Wiki] [Local narrative text]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 88/100 | Autocracy 92/100 | Magic–Artifice 97/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 96/100) | Pluralism 20/100. Phase shift: Winter Court defense and Immarel's rise (Expansion 73, Autocracy 74, magic–artifice intensity 75, Pluralism 35) → lich rule, the Red Winter, and eternal winter (Expansion 91, Autocracy 96, magic–artifice intensity 98, Pluralism 15).

The v2.1 value profile is Evil (26/100), with a worsening trajectory. Phase values: Winter Court survival and defense (Neutral, 49/100) → lich rule and post-disaster expansion east (Evil, 26/100). Defending the country, building hearth cities, and restoring mage education provide public benefits. But the missions explicitly describe purges of opponents, forced assimilation, and the capture of intelligent “cursed” people for camp labor, gravely harming dignity, personhood, and restraint. War, theocracy, lichdom, and undead troops are not themselves grounds for a negative score. The weighted four-dimension result is 26.3, rounded to 26; the headline score represents Immarel's lich route and does not summarize the optional H21 formation diversion. The Chinese source repeats the same phase comparison: Winter Court survival and defense (Neutral, 49/100) → lich rule and post-disaster expansion east (Evil, 26/100). The country suits players who enjoy character-driven tragedy, winter magic, disaster survival, fortification and financial planning, and a long conquest narrative. Expect a punishing campaign if you dislike severe disasters, persistent upkeep, or a state whose protective ambitions turn toward autocracy and forced labor. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

See the evidence record for source locations, fixed Wiki revisions, and unresolved points.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Gemradcurt Traditions

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Core-creation cost: -10% (core_creation; raw value -0.1).

  • Female advisor chance: +10% (female_advisor_chance; raw value 0.10).

1. Immarel Winterswrath

Cornered and driven into desperation by the all-conquering Hibernal Crusade, Gemradcurt fell into political chaos. Were it not for the intervention of the Strutmari Peitar the Winter Court would have been lost, but to the Gemradcurters it was Immarel Winterswrath who saved the realm. Admitted to the Taigan Order and an extraordinarily young age of five, Immarel impressed and soon humbled the high-court druids with her near limitless Wintry magic. Growing up during war with the Autumnal fanatics, Immarel became embittered and resentful, unlike the peaceful patient norm of the Winter Court.

Recognizing her potential, the militarists of Gemradcurt nurtured her rage, and at the age of 11 she had bested the previous Sonad in single combat after becoming frustrated with his inability to combat the Hibernal Crusaders. Immarel and the militarists seized control of the Winter Court, and soon drove out the invaders, ending their advance northward. It is whispered that she had channeled forbidden magic of necromancy, raising shambling corpses to fight, but those rumors are discouraged in the new Winter Court where Immarel reigns supreme.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

2. Glacial Bulwarks

The frigid lands of the Winter Court were home to magnificent fortresses of ice, carved through primordial glaciers and maintained through careful magic. These natural fortifications protected the Snecboth from harm in their icy embrace during the Hibernal Crusade, stalling their advance until Immarel Winterswrath's counterattack. It is said that not even the fiercest of fire could melt the pure blue gleaming ice, much to the dismay of the Autumnal mages who tried with all their magical might to thaw these bastions.

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

3. The Taigan Order

The Winter Court in Gemradcurt was organized into a myriad of bureaucratic orders, each focusing on one aspect of governance and holy duties. The Taigan Order, dedicated to finding and teaching young women with magical talent, was considered to be of lowly stature prior to Immarel Winterswrath's reforms.

With her seizure of governance during the Hibernal Crusade, the pacifist Moraine and Tarn Orders, blamed for their inability to defend the Court, were disbanded and their duties transferred to the Taigan Order who now acted in control of Gemradcurt at only Immarel's orders. The traditional course of action, debate among the different Orders, was henceforth unable to check the Sonad's governance.

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -15% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.15).

4. Collath

Despite the turmoil of the Hibernal Crusade, Gemradcurt and the Winter Court have traditionally followed pacifist tenets, preferring patience and understanding over rash action. Embodying this virtue is the game Collath, a lengthy game of strategy designed to distract from the hardships of Winter and promote camaraderie amongst players.

Said to have been created by early Eordan settlers wishing to spend time while waiting to return to the Domandrod, it is now customary for Gemradcurt theocrats to engage in a friendly match to calm spirits before entering into debate.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

5. Boggfishing

Although the lands were often stark and bare, especially so in the winter, the cold cannot drive all life from the land. Underneath the ice coating the many lakes, streams, and seas life could be found in abundance. The Snecboth rite of passage involves the first ice-fishing trip of an adolescent, often traveling to the seemingly endless Gemradbogg and Murdbogg.

Between the churning waves of the Randrunnse and the frosty pines of the interior, the lowland swamps host a mix of fresh and saltwater which fertilizes the frigid environment. Fishers carefully traverse the ice looking for a deep pool with connections to streams and sea, and cut holes into the ice where they lure underwater creatures.

  • Army maintenance modifier: -5% (land_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.05).

  • Army attrition: -10% (land_attrition; raw value -0.1).

6. Keepers of the Eigras Gate

'While the frozen forests may be labyrinthine to foreign invaders, Eordand is surrounded by the seas that they are familiar with. It is not enough to patrol our lands, for they may strike at any moment, wishing to steal our heirlooms and bespoil Winter's majesty! The Eigras Gate will be guarded: not with walls with archers or fast-striking riders, but with vessels of our own. Gemradcurt will act as the shield of Eordand from these Cannorians, we will close the Eigras Gate with iceberg and warship until they have acknowledged our sovereignty!'

  • excerpt from the debate 'On Foreign Policy and Actions Regarding the Eastern Trespassers'

  • Ship Cost: -10% (global_ship_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. Heart of Winter

In the waning centuries of Eordan rule in the Randrunnse, Gemradcurt dealt with foreign dignitaries with cold but fair attention. Permitting only their diplomats access, Gemradcurt remained closed to the Cannorian world and enforced this with vigilance and might. All nations, no matter how insignificant or grand, are expected to honor the Winter Court's right of supremacy over the north.

In exchange, the pleas and requests of the foreigners may be heard and recorded. Preferring to remain neutral in all conflicts, Gemradcurt has become reliable to Cannorian courts for a mediator between conflicts in Northern Aelantir.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).
